sections.label: Rising checkpoint traveller volumes
sections.summary: Traveller volumes at checkpoints are increasing, with over 200 million people expected yearly through air, land and sea checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, traveller volumes at our various checkpoints have been increasing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We now expect over 200 million people to go through our air, land and sea checkpoints each year.

sections.label: New section 51AA powers
sections.summary: Clause 4 introduces section 51AA giving ICA officers enhanced search, seizure, arrest and security screening powers in Authorised Areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill introduces a new section 51AA, which will provide ICA officers with enhanced powers relating to search and seizure, arrest and security screening, within or in the vicinity of Authorised Areas.

sections.label: Search powers for officers
sections.summary: Clause 4 expands powers allowing ICA and Police Officers to search individuals suspected of offences in or near Authorised Areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 4 will, therefore, expand and allow ICA officers and Police Officers to search individuals if there is suspicion of the commission of any offence within or in the vicinity of the Authorised Areas.

sections.label: Arrest handover and identifiers
sections.summary: Arrested persons must be handed to Police quickly; Clause 5 lets ICA collect identifiers from transit travellers and visa applicants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under the new section 51AA (12), once ICA officers have made an arrest, they will have to hand over the accused to a Police Officer as quickly as possible for the Police to commence their investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill amends section 55(1)(ga) to allow ICA to collect personal identifiers, such as photographs, from travellers transiting through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5 will also make clear that ICA has the powers to collect personal identifiers from Singapore visa applicants, including photographs and other biometric identifiers.

sections.label: Increased penalty quantum
sections.summary: Clause 5 amends section 55(1)(k) to raise maximum prescribed penalties to two years' imprisonment, $3,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill will thus amend section 55(1)(k) of the IA to increase the maximum quantum of penalties that the Minister may prescribe for the breach of regulations, to an imprisonment term not exceeding two years, or a fine not exceeding $3,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will align the maximum penalties for breaches of regulations under the IA with that under NRA.

sections.label: ICA officer authorities under Bill
sections.summary: ICA officers may perform security screenings, search, seize, arrest, respond to incidents, investigate preliminarily, and collect personal identifiers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, ICA officers will have the authority to perform security screenings, carry out search and seizure duties and arrest suspects within and in the vicinity of immigration checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: They would also be able to respond to incidents, conduct preliminary investigations and take steps to contain the situation when Police Officers are not yet at the scene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill will also allow ICA officers to collect personal identifiers, such as photographs, passport details and fingerprints.

sections.label: ICA and Police starting salaries
sections.summary: It states starting monthly salaries for Direct-Entry Sergeants in ICA and the Police Force, and says the amendments empower ICA officers against cross-border threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The starting monthly salary for a Higher National Institute of Technical Education Certificate (NITEC)/NITEC/GCE "O" level qualified Direct-Entry Sergeant in ICA is between $1,670 to $1,880 per month, while the starting monthly salary for a Higher NITEC/NITEC/GCE "O" level qualified Direct-Entry Sergeant in the Police Force is between $1,820 and $2,170 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendments provide greater empowerment to ICA officers critical in dealing with any cross-border threats.

sections.label: ICA officer arrest powers
sections.summary: It states that under new section 51AA subsection 10(b), an ICA officer may use all reasonable means necessary to make an arrest if the person resists or evades.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the inclusion of the new section 51AA, subsection 10(b), the ICA officer may use all reasonable means necessary to make the arrest if the person to be arrested forcibly resists or tries to evade the arrest.

sections.label: ICA arrest and police handover
sections.summary: It says training aids security, efficiency and morale, but notes ICA officers must inform Police of an arrest and wait to hand over the suspect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the relevant training that comes with these new duties, this will not only aid in improving security and efficiency, it can boost the officers' morale as they can carry out their tasks more efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I note that when a suspect is arrested by ICA, the ICA officer is required to inform a Police Officer of the arrest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And he has to wait for the arrival of the Police to hand over the suspect under section 51AA, clause 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And why cannot ICA be given the authority to detain the suspect for investigation for more than 24 hours and carry out whatever investigations required if it is a simple offence.

sections.label: ICA statement-taking powers
sections.summary: It states the amendments give ICA officers power to take statements from persons who appear acquainted with the facts and circumstances of relevant offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments will give ICA officers the power to take statements from persons who appear to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the relevant offences.

sections.label: Adverse inferences from silence
sections.summary: It asks whether adverse inferences can be drawn from a statement taken under section 51AA(5) if the person chooses to remain silent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I clarify whether adverse inferences can be drawn from a statement taken under section 51AA(5) should the person choose to remain silent?

sections.label: Admissibility of statements
sections.summary: It asks whether failure to comply with the requirements under section 51AA(7) affects the admissibility of the statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will a failure to comply with the requirements under section 51AA(7) affect the admissibility of the statement?

sections.label: ICA 24-hour detention power
sections.summary: Asks whether ICA officers need power to detain a person up to 24 hours before handing them to a Police Officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, is it necessary for ICA officers to be given the power to detain a person for up to 24 hours under section 51AA(12) before handing them over to a Police Officer?

sections.label: ICA stop and search powers
sections.summary: New section 51AA(1) and (2) in clause 4 lets ICA officers stop and search vehicles, trains, vessels, persons or aircraft for evidence of criminal offences in or around the protected area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The new section 51AA (1) and (2) under clause 4 of the Bill seeks to allow ICA officers to stop and search any vehicle, train, vessel or person or any aircraft for evidence of criminal offences being committed in or around the protected area.

sections.label: Arrest handover to Police
sections.summary: Subsection (12) requires the ICA officer to inform Police immediately of the arrest, await their arrival for handover, and detain the person in a suitable place not more than 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Subsection (12) requires the ICA officer to inform the Police immediately of the arrest and await the Police's arrival for handover, detaining the person in a suitable place for not more than 24 hours.

sections.label: Interpol lost travel documents
sections.summary: As of July 2013, Interpol had nearly 38 million lost or stolen travel documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As of July 2013, Interpol had nearly 38 million lost or stolen travel documents.

sections.label: APEC counter-terrorism travel commitments
sections.summary: The collection of personal identifiers adds to Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record programmes Singapore committed to in the 2016 APEC counter-terrorism action plan in October last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The collection of personal identifiers adds to the Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record programmes which Singapore had committed in the 2016 Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) counter-terrorism action plan in October last year to secure and facilitate legitimate travel within the region.

sections.label: Clause 55B personal identifiers
sections.summary: Clause 55B, providing for collection of personal identifiers, covers those in transit and those who apply for or hold a Singapore visa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 55B, which provides for collection of personal identifiers, covers both those who remain in transit and those who apply for or hold a Singapore visa.

sections.label: Travellers and personal identifiers
sections.summary: As airport traveller numbers hit a record 60 million last year, legitimate travellers should not fear collection of personal identifiers like fingerprints and irises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the number of travellers at our airports has been increasing, hitting the record 60 million mark last year, it is important that those who travel through Singapore for legitimate reasons not be afraid of the collection of important personal identifiers, such as fingerprints and even irises.

sections.label: Bill raises penalties, airport passenger numbers
sections.summary: Clause 5(C) raises the penalty to two years' imprisonment or a $3,000 fine, and Changi Airport handled over 50 million passengers last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Originally set at imprisonment of six months or a fine of $1,000, clause 5(C) of this present Bill increases it to imprisonment of two years or a fine of $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By empowering Home Team officers to respond promptly and by enhancing security measures, this Bill is a further step forward towards a synergistic and comprehensive move against terror threats in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: During festive periods, the numbers can go up to half a million a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Changi Airport handled more than 50 million passengers last year and looks set to increase its passenger load with Terminal 5 (T5) on the way.

sections.label: ICA officers' search and arrest powers
sections.summary: The Bill widens ICA officers' powers to search and arrest suspects for some offences currently under Police authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With Singapore seeking to continue our position as a top transit hub, we must be at the top of the game with our security without losing our hallmark efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill widens the powers of ICA officers to search and arrest suspects for some offences, which currently come under the authority of the Police.

sections.label: ICA collecting transit travellers' identifiers
sections.summary: The Bill allows ICA to collect personal identifiers from travellers in transit at Changi Airport where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One important measure included in this Bill is to allow ICA to collect personal identifiers from travellers in transit at Changi Airport where necessary.

sections.label: Checkpoints clustered into three domains
sections.summary: Under the ICC, checkpoints are clustered into three domains: Land, Sea and Air, progressively launched in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under the ICC, the checkpoints are clustered into three domains, namely, the Land Domain, Sea Domain and Air Domain, which were progressively launched in 2015.

sections.label: Woodlands operation detected ISIS-bound travellers
sections.summary: In 2016, a joint operation at Woodlands Checkpoint detected four male Indonesian travellers planning to enter Singapore to fight for ISIS.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, a joint operation at Woodlands Checkpoint detected four male Indonesian travellers who had plans to enter Singapore to make their way to Syria to fight for the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS).

sections.label: Exercise Northstar at Changi Airport
sections.summary: Exercise Northstar in October 2017 at Changi Airport involved Home Team agencies, the SAF, MOH, CAAS and CAG.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, Exercise Northstar, held in October 2017 at Changi Airport, involved Home Team agencies as well as the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), the Ministry of Health (MOH), Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and Changi Airport Group (CAG).

sections.label: ICA officer training and guidelines
sections.summary: Over 900 ICA officers have undergone training, and ICA will progressively cover all selected for protective security duties and issue guidelines on enhanced powers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, more than 900 ICA officers have undergone the training and ICA will progressively cover all those selected for protective security duties.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Besides training, ICA will issue guidelines and directives to ICA officers on the proper exercise of their enhanced powers, similar to directives and orders governing Police Officers today.

sections.label: ICA officer 24-hour detention
sections.summary: The provision allows an ICA officer to detain the person for up to 24 hours to cater to such circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To cater to such circumstances, the provision allows an ICA officer to detain the person for up to 24 hours.

sections.label: New section modelled after CPC
sections.summary: The new section 51AA(5) to (7) of the Bill is modelled after section 22 of the CPC, not section 23.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On this basis, the new section 51AA(5) to (7) of the Bill is modelled after section 22 of the CPC, rather than section 23.

sections.label: Reasonableness in using force
sections.summary: Reasonableness generally entails using only as much force as is appropriate to effect arrest and proportional to the perceived threat.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Generally speaking, reasonableness will entail using only as much force as is appropriate to effect arrest and one that is proportional to the level of the perceived threat.

sections.label: Reviewing Home Team officer salaries
sections.summary: MHA regularly reviews salaries of Home Team officers, including ICA and SPF officers, to keep them competitive given job demands, risks and skills.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MHA regularly reviews the salaries of Home Team officers, including ICA and SPF officers, to ensure that they remain competitive, taking into account the job demands, the risks, as well as specialised skills requirements.

sections.label: New scheme for senior ranks
sections.summary: A new scheme was introduced in July last year to give officers more seamless progression into senior ranks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As recently as July last year, a new scheme was introduced to provide officers with a more seamless progression into the senior ranks.

sections.label: Screening transit passengers against INTERPOL database
sections.summary: Passport information of selected transit passengers will be screened against INTERPOL's Stolen and Lost Travel Documents database, which has 38 million entries.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On cross-border collaboration, passport information of selected transit passengers will be screened against the Stolen and Lost Travel Documents (SLTD) database, which is an international database administered by the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) and, as Mr Christopher de Souza informed us, that database is a long one.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It has 38 million entries, and we will screen selectively against this database.
